issues.legal_issue: Members of an unlawful assembly may be convicted vicariously of grievous hurt even when a member’s act caused death and no person was convicted of the standalone grievous-hurt offence.
material_facts: The courts below found that the convicted accused formed an unlawful assembly whose common object was to cause grievous hurt, and that its members knew grievous hurt was likely in pursuit of that object.
One member caused the deaths of two people; the other members were found not responsible for the deaths.
The principal offender was convicted of murder, while the other convicted members were convicted of grievous hurt with the aid of the rule of unlawful-assembly liability.
No person was convicted of the standalone grievous-hurt offence.
The Supreme Court accepted the factual findings because no procedural illegality, unfair trial, or gross miscarriage of justice was shown.
issues.conclusion: The convictions of the other members for grievous hurt through unlawful-assembly liability were legally sustainable, despite the murder conviction of the principal offender and the absence of a standalone grievous-hurt conviction; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code imposes vicarious liability for an offence committed in prosecution of an unlawful assembly’s common object, or for an offence members knew was likely to be committed in prosecution of that object. Members’ knowledge and liability may differ. Grievous hurt is a minor offence in relation to murder, so the fact that a member committed murder does not prevent other members from being convicted of grievous hurt on the basis of the assembly’s object and their knowledge. The Court relied on Jahiruddin v. Queen Empress, ILR 22 Cal 306, and the approach in Bhagwat Singh v. Emperor, AIR 1936 Pat 481, and Sidhu Gope v. Emperor, AIR 1946 Pat 84; it rejected the contrary view in Ram Prasad Singh v. King Emperor, ILR 1 Pat 753 (AIR 1923 Pat 50), and distinguished Queen v. Sabid Ali, 20 Suth WR Cr 5 (FB).

rule.if: criminal_appeal and unlawful_assembly and common_object_grievous_hurt and members_knew_grievous_hurt_likely and one_member_caused_death and other_members_not_liable_for_death and no_member_convicted_of_standalone_grievous_hurt

predicates.criminal_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a criminal case.
predicates.unlawful_assembly: The accused formed an unlawful assembly.
predicates.common_object_grievous_hurt: The assembly's common object was to cause grievous hurt.
predicates.members_knew_grievous_hurt_likely: The members knew grievous hurt was likely to be caused in pursuit of the assembly's common object.
predicates.one_member_caused_death: One member of the assembly caused a person's death.
predicates.other_members_not_liable_for_death: The other members were found not responsible for the death-causing offence.
predicates.no_member_convicted_of_standalone_grievo: No member was convicted of the standalone grievous-hurt offence.

issues.definition: When an unlawful assembly in a criminal appeal shared the object of causing grievous hurt and its members knew that harm was likely, a member's death-causing act and the absence of a standalone grievous-hurt conviction do not prevent the other members from being held vicariously liable for grievous hurt if they were not liable for the death-causing offence.
